summary: Counterfactual conditionals on finite ordering models. Truth at every closest antecedent-world agrees with Lewis's general truth condition; modus ponens holds under weak centering; conditional excluded middle holds under Stalnaker's assumption and fails without it; strengthening the antecedent, transitivity and contraposition fail on a four-world model of the Sobel sequence. In von Fintel's dynamic account the Sobel sequence is accepted in one order and rejected in the reverse.

theorems.name: would_iff_lewis
theorems.source_claim: T1. On a finite model the closest-worlds condition and Lewis's general condition agree. Lewis p. 20: under the Limit Assumption the truth conditions simplify in this way.

theorems.name: might_dual
theorems.source_claim: T2. 'might' is the dual of 'would'. Lewis p. 21 takes this as the definition of 'might' and derives the closest-worlds condition; here the closest-worlds condition is the definition and the duality is derived.

theorems.name: vacuous_truth
theorems.source_claim: T3. If there is no antecedent-world, 'would' is vacuously true and 'might' is false. Lewis p. 16 (the vacuous case), p. 22 (might).

theorems.name: modus_ponens
theorems.source_claim: T4. Modus ponens for 'would' under weak centering. Lewis p. 27 states the pattern; p. 29 says it survives the retreat to weak centering.

theorems.name: centering_and
theorems.source_claim: T5. Under centering a true antecedent and a true consequent give a true counterfactual. Lewis p. 26, the second of the two inference-patterns at the foot of the page; p. 29 says it is lost under weak centering.

theorems.name: cem_stalnaker
theorems.source_claim: T6. Conditional Excluded Middle under Stalnaker's Assumption. Lewis p. 79.

theorems.name: cem_stalnaker_at
theorems.source_claim: T6'. Conditional Excluded Middle for one antecedent, from Stalnaker's Assumption at that antecedent. Lewis pp. 78-79.

theorems.name: stalnaker_linear_implies_at
theorems.source_claim: ours: the linear form implies the assumption at every antecedent.

theorems.name: restricted_transitivity
theorems.source_claim: T7. The valid special case of transitivity. Lewis p. 35, the simplified pattern: from X []-> A and (X & A) []-> C infer X []-> C.

theorems.name: vf_null_context
theorems.source_claim: T8. In the null context, where the horizon at i is just {i}, the dynamic conditional has the same truth value as 'would'. von Fintel p. 139 ("does not lead to a difference in the truth-conditions derived for an isolated...

theorems.name: vf_decompose
theorems.source_claim: ours: the dynamic conditional is the Lewis conditional together with a strict conditional over the worlds already in the horizon.

theorems.name: sobel_sequence
theorems.source_claim: The Sobel sequence, von Fintel (10) p. 130; Lewis p. 10: both sentences are true at actual, together with the negated opposite of the second.

theorems.name: model_centered
theorems.source_claim: The premises of T3, T4, T5, T8 are satisfiable: the model is centered (hence weakly centered) on actual, and 'never' has no worlds.

theorems.name: restricted_transitivity_instance
theorems.source_claim: T7 at work: all []-> usa and (all & usa) []-> peace, so all []-> peace.

theorems.name: strengthening_fails
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 1. Strengthening the antecedent fails (Lewis p. 31): usa []-> war, but not (usa & all) []-> war.

theorems.name: transitivity_fails
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 2. Transitivity fails (Lewis p. 32): all []-> usa and usa []-> war, but not all []-> war.

theorems.name: contraposition_fails
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 3. Contraposition fails (Lewis p. 35): usa []-> not all, but not (all []-> not usa).

theorems.name: cem_fails
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 4. Conditional Excluded Middle fails when two closest antecedent-worlds are tied (Lewis p. 80: comparative similarity permits ties): neither usa []-> odd nor usa []-> not odd.

theorems.name: model_not_stalnaker
theorems.source_claim: Hence the model does not satisfy Stalnaker's Assumption at actual.
